newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse weaker in lower turnover.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse weaker in lower turnover.

text.p: The Bucharest bourse eased on Wednesday due to losses among first-tier heavyweights under selling pressure, traders said.
"Buyers were almost absent and that triggered lower prices and turnover," one broker said. He added that small cap stocks' lack of liquidity had also affected investors' buying mood.

Bourse operators said the market was now in a correction phase and expected further declines throughout the summer period. Some traders said occasional rises might occur on demand for high caps but the downtrend would persist.
Traders forecast a new bullish mood in September, with buyers stepping into the market.
On Wednesday, average prices of 29 stocks fell and 19 rose. Two companies were suspended, while one had no trade.
Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, fell by 2.6, 2.41 and 2.59 percent respectively from Monday.
On the first tier, five listings closed weaker, one rose, and one was flat. Refrigerator manufacturer Arctic remained suspended.
Pharmaceutical Terapia ended 400 lei higher at 8,900 amid strong demand, but Antibiotice another drug maker listed on the first tier was 200 lei weaker at 7,300.
Chemical plant Oltchim was flat at 3,900. One trader said the price could slide to a support level of 3,700.
The second tier remained affected by poor liquidity among small stocks. Traders expected no improvement until September.
The bourse reported three post-session special deals struck outside the market worth 785.5 billion lei.

One special deal was in first-tier listing spare cars maker Compa involving 143,102 shares worth 405.02 million lei. A second, with 184,930 shares totalling 279.98 million lei was in oil equipment manufacturer Ciprom.
A third deal involved 60,256 shares in ceramic products maker Apcarom, worth 100.5 million lei.
Overall turnover, including special deals, fell to 7.03 billion lei from 8.6 billion previously.
